title: Inferred constexpr bindings use double colon and named constants use compile-time purple
summary: constexpr auto displays as name :: value, while constexpr declaration names and k_ identifiers carry a dedicated purple constant role.
details: Both constexpr auto k_limit{value}; and constexpr auto k_limit = value; display as k_limit :: value; the redundant auto placeholder is omitted.
Ordinary inferred assignments retain name := value, while an explicit compile-time type retains name: Type : value.
A recognized constexpr declaration colors its displayed binding name with DansConstant even when the source name has not yet adopted the convention.

The owner's k_ prefix identifies named constants at every raw and overlaid use site, including expressions and non-type template arguments where declaration-local constexpr parsing cannot propagate identity.
DansConstant is a distinct rethemable role using the existing compile-time purple #bb9af7; strings, comments, includes, and gray static assertions retain their higher-priority context colors.
Cursor and Visual reveal show exact C++ source, source bytes and row identity remain unchanged, and the selected profile is the production default.

The compared double-colon, colon-equals, and visible-auto spellings remain validated buffer-local profiles; the selected style-lab catalog hash is 83410ae5b51c219861a4b0b62be4308dc21dea0697f9bd3c4901f362dac58c51.
rationale: Double colon makes an inferred compile-time binding textually distinct from the established colon-equals runtime assignment.
Displaying auto adds no type information, while a concrete written type remains useful and therefore stays visible.
The k_ convention carries constant identity to references without depending on LSP semantic-token coloring, which the frontend deliberately disables.
Reusing the macro/compile-time purple keeps the palette small, while a separate highlight group preserves future retheming freedom.
alternatives: Use name := value for constexpr auto; rejected because := already denotes ordinary inferred assignments.
Keep name: auto : value; rejected because the placeholder is redundant and visually noisy.
Color only declaration sites discovered through constexpr parsing; rejected because uses would lose constant identity, while the established k_ convention supplies it directly.

provenance.note: Owner chose double colon after noting that colon-equals already serves ordinary assignments, and identified k_ as the constant-name prefix.

provenance.reference: lua/custom/dans_frontend_cpp/render.lua, parse.lua, markers.lua, highlights.lua, and style.lua

evidence.claim: Brace/equal spelling, concrete-type control, declaration/use/template/string colors, raw match registration, exact RGB value, and integrated output are pinned.
Real Visual reveal/restore, source integrity, selected spelling, constant color restoration, and simultaneous buffer-local alternatives are deterministic.
Embedded Neovim ext_linegrid captures validate all three profiles, unchanged controls and source, and the selected purple constant run.

questions: Why does constexpr use double colon instead of colon equals?
What color are k_ constants and their uses?
Does an unprefixed constexpr declaration still receive the constant color?

last_verified.method: Superseded by the owner's same-day clarification that k_ should be concealed and its visible name tail should use a restrained yellow-orange; DEC-020 retains the double-colon portion of this choice.
